2026-11-02.headline: 从涨落与拓扑到材料设计：多尺度建模与量子模拟的交叉进展
2026-11-02.overview: 本期论文覆盖统计物理涨落理论、量子纠错与拓扑物态、第一性原理与机器学习辅助材料建模、活性物质与软物质动力学，以及量子模拟与量子几何等方向。共同问题在于如何在有限尺寸、非平衡或强关联条件下，从微观模型可靠地提取可观测的宏观量或相行为；不同路线包括严格解析与形式化推导、张量网络与量子蒙特卡洛等数值方法、以及代理模型与生成式设计等数据驱动手段。多数结果仍处于理论、模拟或小体系验证阶段，跨论文之间不宜直接比较或外推。

themes.title: 涨落、弛豫与输运的理论刻画
themes.summary: 多篇工作从不同角度处理非平衡或有限振幅下的弛豫与输运：将Mpemba效应表述为熵产生竞赛并给出有限振幅交叉时间界；在无相互作用费米子中给出淬火谱形状因子对数的Airy分布并指出失去自平均；用张量网络推广密度矩阵截断以预测高维高温输运系数；以及从平衡热力学性质无拟合参数预测Lennard-Jones流体热导率。这些结果分别限定在特定模型、维度或参数区间。

themes.title: 拓扑物态、量子纠错与量子模拟
themes.summary: 拓扑与量子信息方向包含多条具体证据：对称性增强环面码在独立比特翻转与相位翻转噪声下顶点综合征阈值较环面码提高30%；在4×4超导量子比特环面上制备Laughlin-like玻色子分数量子陈绝缘体基态及双准空穴态；单个电感分流磁通量子比特被解析映射为扩展SSH链并数值确认手征对称性保护的边缘态；以及学习型量子LDPC解码器跨码族与噪声模型迁移的报道。这些结果分别受限于特定噪声信道、小体系或模拟条件。

themes.title: 第一性原理与数据驱动的材料建模
themes.summary: 材料建模方面，SKFitter从第一性原理构建对称分辨Slater-Koster紧束缚模型，在八个材料中费米能级1 eV内能带误差9-41 meV；全势KKR用于SiGeSn合金，给出晶格参数偏离Vegard定律与混合焓；ORCHID将文献有限温度热力学证据结构化并接入CALPHAD评估，在Cu-Zr上报告不变温度恢复；代理模型引导的智能体搜索在位点无序晶体中报告94%成功率。各方法的验证体系与误差口径不同。

themes.title: 活性物质、软物质与界面动力学
themes.summary: 活性与软物质方向给出多种微观机制：活体手性流体随密度升高形成旋转小簇并合并为逾渗手性流体，单细胞顺时针自旋而簇逆时针公转；椭球形Quincke滚子中横向推进使极性速度场与垂直向列取向共存，出现整数+1速度涡旋与-1鞍形缺陷；微游泳体自利适应导致成对收益低于各自单独游动；干燥动力学在粘弹性薄膜上选择开放蜂窝折叠网络，波长随膜厚呈5/8幂律。结论多基于模型或特定实验体系。

themes.title: 量子几何、磁性劈裂与光谱探测
themes.summary: 量子几何与磁性方向包含：在KV2Se2O中Berry曲率四极贡献正比于τ²的三阶非线性霍尔响应；PT对称反铁磁体中存在由带间厄米联络实部主导的亚带隙二次谐波产生且符号随Néel序反转；α-MnTe外延层在90 K下ARPES显示Γ-K方向约300 meV、Γ-M方向约150 meV的各向异性价带劈裂；以及圆偏振光驱动石墨烯中观测到光致能隙并被指认为Haldane质量。各结果分别依赖对称性论证、特定测量温度或光谱指认。

2026-11-02.caveat: 阅读时需核对：多数结果为摘要层面的理论、模拟或小体系验证，未给出完整误差、参数范围与有限尺寸分析；部分数值（如阈值提高30%、F1=0.92、能带误差9-41 meV、Tc≈0.7 K、成功率94%）对应特定体系或条件，不能外推到其他材料或噪声模型；形式化推导、平均场、谐波近似、单螺旋度约化等结论需核对适用边界；涉及AI辅助生成证明或代理模型的工作应核对验证完备性；摘要未给出的实验条件、样品参数与统计细节需查全文。

2026-10-30.headline: 从谱与拓扑到有限温度：多尺度物性调控的几条路径
2026-10-30.overview: 本期论文覆盖量子多体与拓扑、超导与磁性材料、软物质与活性输运、以及机器学习辅助材料计算等方向。共同问题集中在：如何用谱结构、对称性与有效理论刻画相与响应，以及有限温度、无序和驱动如何改变这些刻画。不同路线包括严格解析与场论构造、数值模拟与量子蒙特卡洛、以及数据驱动代理模型与自动建模。多数结果仍属理论或有限体系验证，实验类工作多限于特定样品与条件。

themes.title: 谱映射、拓扑不变量与对称性约束
themes.summary: 多篇工作把谱或对称性作为统一语言：算符QSVT给出谱映射并指出核扇区拓扑指数在相位选择与保隙形变下不变；2-群对称性的格点定义把混合对称反常化为Postnikov类；自旋空间对称性用母空间群实表示替代自旋空间群，把磁响应允许条件统一为表示外幂与多极表示的重叠；紧束缚图上完整直流霍尔响应在杂质散射下与轨道几何嵌入无关。这些结果共同显示谱与表示论约束可跨模型组织响应，但各自适用条件不同。

themes.title: 超导配对与磁序的竞争和共存
themes.summary: 超导相关论文从不同机制切入：B1g声子与排斥Hubbard模型协同产生d波超导，转变温度高于单独相互作用；自旋不平衡BCS泛函中证明一阶相变，共存耦合低于正常态线性稳定阈值；单层Fe(Te,Se)的约瑟夫森隧道呈半晶胞周期调制，与符号反转无节点d波一致；BaFe2S3中长程条纹反铁磁序与超导共存，局域铁磁矩被抑制近80%；La4Ni3O3O10中双轴压应力把密度波相与零电阻态分离。这些证据指向配对与磁序/密度波之间的竞争或共存，但材料与参数范围各异。

themes.title: 有限温度、无序与驱动下的拓扑与输运
themes.summary: 长程环相互作用可在二维toric code中实现有限温度任意子禁闭与拓扑序；非厄米IAAF模型中虚相位移动决定周期级联离域转变的周期；准周期Aubry-André-Harper晶格中临界与局域模式导致发射体非马尔可夫动力学与束缚态；拓扑三临界点使边界模呈线性包络无标度衰减；漂移偏置石墨烯中像极化激元产生方向性近场发射与约40%左右不对称度。这些工作把拓扑或局域化概念放到有限温度、非厄米与驱动条件下检验，结论多依赖模型参数。

themes.title: 软物质、活性与随机动力学中的几何控制
themes.summary: 近晶液晶环形焦锥畴阵列中活性粒子输运由内禀持续与缺陷散射涌现持续两种机制竞争；DNA液滴/肌动蛋白复合物在体积分数不足10%时使网络可逆增刚约25倍；带电泳动体周围离子云在较高活性下中距离先幂律后拉伸指数衰减，远处恢复指数屏蔽但屏蔽长度增大；局域随机过程维持长程条件互信息稳态需付出熵产生下界σ̂≥cξ²；纳米颗粒crowding促进凝胶去溶胀并限制crowder负载容量。共同点是几何或局域约束如何决定宏观输运与力学响应。

themes.title: 机器学习辅助的材料建模与谱计算
themes.summary: MoireKP从局域轨道从头算哈密顿量自动构建对称性约束连续模型，高对称k路径目标窗口内误差在3.0 meV以内；ML-COHP用MACE冻结描述符预测ICOHP，强键误差约1.6–4.1%，耗时约1秒而LOBSTER需5–51小时；知识蒸馏把大型MLIP迁移到约快40倍的学生模型，数天内产生稳定20 ns电解质轨迹；Crystoria数据集含2,649,640个结构，其中67.68%判为动力学稳定；nn-EQL在稀疏高维材料数据中生成并排序候选方程。这些工作共同处理精度、速度与可解释性的权衡，但定量验证多限于所测体系。

2026-10-30.caveat: 阅读时需核对：各理论工作的适用参数范围、近似阶数与有限尺寸效应；实验工作的样品制备、温度/压力/场强条件与统计不确定度；机器学习模型的训练集覆盖、误差统计与泛化边界；部分PRB条目摘要被截断，不能据片段推断完整结论；所有数值与比例均以摘要给出为准，未给出的数字不应补推。

2026-10-28.headline: 从非平衡稳态到可计算框架：多体系中的关联、相变与算法进展
2026-10-28.overview: 本期论文覆盖凝聚态、统计物理、量子信息与材料计算等多个方向，共同关注如何在复杂或非平衡条件下刻画关联与相变：有的从局域场因子、对称性分辨或条件互信息入手修正或扩展既有描述；有的借助精确可解模型、复制方法与蒙特卡洛给出可控判据；还有多篇聚焦机器学习与数值算法，用于逆问题、哈密顿量学习和可合成性预测。路线差异明显：解析场论、精确对角化、分子模拟与数据驱动方法并行，彼此多为方法层面的呼应而非同一物理结论。

themes.title: 关联与涨落的精细刻画
themes.summary: 多篇工作表明，仅凭平均量或单一关联函数不足以描述体系。电子气中同自旋关联削减交换峰约一半，并与QMC及q=0压缩率、自旋磁化率一致；部分观测临界系统中存在由单一平衡构型导致的误差下限R_n，二维Ising磁化下限约0.072；经典随机动力学中条件互信息在马尔可夫长度发散时呈普适标度，固定区域标度维度为2。这些结果共同强调关联结构对可观测量的约束，但各自模型与适用条件不同。

themes.title: 简并、对称性与拓扑态的判别
themes.summary: 简并基态空间中，不同对称性分辨方式选出关联性质迥异的状态：FeO的Hubbard模型基态为16重简并，局域磁化给出Slater行列式基，总自旋量子数选出纠缠非高斯态；强到弱自发对称破缺可由量子Fisher信息亏损刻画，并与保真度、Rényi-1关联在渐近长程有序诊断上等价；双曲晶格规范-希格斯模型中出现平直空间没有的“群岛”相，其转变属平均场普适类。这些工作提供的是判据与模型结果，尚未统一为单一分类。

themes.title: 非平衡与驱动体系的新稳态
themes.summary: 周期性驱动玻色气体与热浴耦合时，高温态和BEC态均出现涌现费米面，源于非平衡碰撞缺乏细致平衡；耗散里德堡阵列中次近邻阻挫与最近邻补偿竞争，产生液固构型共存的动力学雪泥相，并伴随分形团簇与广义Ornstein-Zernike关联；平均场Ising博弈的大种群稳态Nash平衡满足细致平衡且呈Gibbs形式，铁磁情形随温度降低发生二阶相变。三者的非平衡机制与可观测量各异，不宜直接类比。

themes.title: 面向复杂体系的计算与学习框架
themes.summary: ODAT-SE 4.0通过统一接口解耦优化/采样算法与求解器，提供两级MPI并行、检查点续算与贝叶斯工作流，并以线性回归闭式解和正电子衍射示例验证；UniTB在跨68种元素的非磁测试晶体上达到0.48 meV矩阵元误差，未用非晶数据训练即与DFT非晶Ge-Sb-Te光学和电导一致；Prospector在半导体制造文献知识图谱上接近同等条件下最强现成模型，并迁移到三个未见图谱。这些进展侧重框架与基准，实际外推边界仍需逐项核对。

themes.title: 材料与器件的可调响应
themes.summary: 双层SiN_x/Al纳米膜通过Al层厚度调节频率-温度转折点，72 nm Al样品在90–300 K呈单调负温度系数，热响应低于1 s；少层T_d-MoTe₂的自旋-轨道散射时间可静电调控至多三倍，单双层均由D'yakonov–Perel'机制主导；Nb₃Sn中随Zr含量增加表面形貌改善、空洞密度下降，最优Zr含量下超导性能提升且表面铌氧化物更薄。三者的调控参量与表征手段不同，均属特定样品与条件下的结果。

2026-10-28.caveat: 阅读时需核对各文的适用边界：电子气结果仅比较rs=1和2及q=0；部分观测临界系统的误差下限依赖关联衰减与采样协议；条件互信息标度限于一维经典随机模型；FeO/Fe₂O₂结论限于特定模型与参数；量子Fisher信息判据限于强Z2对称且具局域带电对合的态；驱动玻色气体与里德堡阵列的驱动参数、维度与温度范围摘要未给出；ODAT-SE、UniTB与Prospector的验证分别限于所列基准、非晶Ge-Sb-Te及特定知识图谱，不能外推为普遍性能；纳米膜仅覆盖90–300 K，MoTe₂的栅压与温度条件未明，Nb₃Sn的最优Zr含量与超导参数数值未给出。所有数字与机制均应以原文为准，不据此推断领域趋势。

papers.title: Resolving the spinon hierarchy of the Heisenberg antiferromagnet
papers.abstract: A local spin fluctuation in the spin-$\tfrac12$ Heisenberg antiferromagnet creates an even number of fractional spinon excitations. We resolve its zero-temperature dynamical structure factor through six spinons directly in the thermodynamic limit. Beyond the established two-spinon contribution of $72.89\%$, the four-spinon response gives approximately $21.90\%$ of the integrated intensity and six spinons contribute a further $4.3\%$, bringing the response to about $99\%$ of both the intensity and first-frequency-moment sum rules. We derive momentum-independent first-moment fractions in the calculated sectors and a general upper-edge law $S_n\sim A_n(k)(ω_{n,u}-ω)^{(n^2-3)/2}$ for every even $n$ at nonzero momentum. The rapid growth of the edge exponent explains why the expanding multiparticle bandwidth carries very little high-energy weight, while higher sectors remain appreciable within the lower-sector continua.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论计算；依据为动力学结构因子的解析/数值求解；研究对象：自旋1/2海森堡反铁磁体（spin-1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnet）
papers.abstract_summary_zh: 在热力学极限下直接解析零温动力学结构因子，六自旋子（six-spinon）响应使强度与一阶频率矩求和规则均达到约99%。
papers.main_content_zh:
研究问题：局域自旋涨落产生的偶数个分数化自旋子（spinon）激发如何分层贡献动力学结构因子，各多自旋子扇区的谱权重与边缘行为如何。
证据与比较：两自旋子贡献72.89%，四自旋子约21.90%积分强度，六自旋子再贡献4.3%，合计约99%的强度与一阶频率矩求和规则；给出所计算扇区中与动量无关的一阶矩分数及非零动量下各偶数n的上边缘律。
papers.method_zh: 在热力学极限下求解零温动力学结构因子，分解至六自旋子扇区并计算强度与频率矩求和规则。

english_guide.finding: Resolving the zero-temperature dynamical structure factor directly in the thermodynamic limit, six-spinon contributions bring the response to about 99% of both the intensity and first-frequency-moment sum rules.
english_guide.question: How do even numbers of fractional spinon excitations created by a local spin fluctuation contribute to the dynamical structure factor, and what are the spectral weights and edge behaviors of the multiparticle sectors?
english_guide.evidence: Two spinons contribute 72.89%, four spinons about 21.90% of the integrated intensity, and six spinons a further 4.3%, totaling about 99% of the intensity and first-moment sum rules; momentum-independent first-moment fractions and a general upper-edge law for every even n at nonzero momentum are derived.
english_guide.method: The zero-temperature dynamical structure factor is resolved through six spinons directly in the thermodynamic limit, with intensity and frequency-moment sum rules computed.
english_guide.novelty: The authors state a direct thermodynamic-limit resolution through six spinons, a general upper-edge law for every even n at nonzero momentum, and momentum-independent first-moment fractions.
english_guide.limitations: The abstract does not specify applicability conditions or approximations; it concerns zero temperature and the spin-1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnet only, with no verifiable information on finite temperature or other models.

papers.novelty_zh: 作者称直接于热力学极限解析至六自旋子，并给出非零动量下所有偶数n的上边缘幂律及动量无关的一阶矩分数。
papers.limitations_zh: 摘要未明确说明适用范围与近似条件；仅涉及零温与自旋1/2海森堡反铁磁体，未提供有限温或其它模型的可核实信息。

papers.title: Observation of light-induced Haldane gap in graphene
papers.abstract: Symmetry and topology, encoded in electronic wavefunctions, play a central role in the electronic properties and emergent phenomena of quantum materials. While these properties are conventionally determined by the equilibrium Hamiltonian, strong optical fields offer a fundamentally different route by reshaping the Hamiltonian on ultrafast timescales, turning symmetry and topology into dynamically controllable degrees of freedom. Graphene provides a paradigmatic platform for realizing this concept, where circularly polarized light has long been predicted to dynamically break time-reversal symmetry (TRS) and open a topologically nontrivial gap at the Dirac point. Despite extensive experimental efforts, direct observation of this Dirac gap-the defining spectroscopic signature of the dynamical TRS-breaking induced topological phase-has remained missing. Here we directly observe this light-induced Dirac gap in monolayer graphene. Time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy reveals that the gap emerges simultaneously with the optical field and exclusively under circularly polarized driving, directly linking its opening to dynamical TRS breaking. Together with Floquet theory, we identify the gap with a light-induced Haldane mass and reveal the associated nontrivial Floquet Berry curvature and Chern topology. By demonstrating dynamical TRS breaking in a prototypical non-magnetic material, our results establish optical driving as a route to ultrafast engineering of symmetry and topology, opening opportunities for dynamically tunable quantum matter beyond equilibrium.

papers.title: Quantum 3xplorer: AI-Native Engine for Next-Generation Quantum Materials Modeling
papers.abstract: Quantum-mechanical approaches, such as density functional theory (DFT), underpin much of modern computational materials science and are the primary source of data for AI-driven discovery. Yet the established electronic-structure codes today represent decades-old software architectures, making new physical models slow and costly to implement, validate, and deploy on emerging hardware. We present Quantum 3xplorer (Q3, pronounced "Quantum Explorer"), an AI-native quantum simulation engine written from scratch by AI coding agents under the direction and supervision of domain scientists. As a first and demanding validation case, we implement plane-wave pseudopotential DFT end to end: norm-conserving, ultrasoft, and projector-augmented-wave formalisms, spin polarization, DFT+U, and dispersion corrections, together with forces, stresses, structural relaxation, and electronic-structure analysis. Q3 reproduces established reference implementations, runs faster on a single core in representative benchmarks, and scales across GPU-accelerated supercomputers. It was developed in weeks rather than years. Its layered, physics-first architecture separates abstract quantum-mechanical concepts from their numerical representations, making its framework extendable beyond plane waves to other basis sets and levels of theory. Its inputs and outputs follow structured, schema-validated data standards, making every result AI-ready. Q3 is open source under Apache 2.0 and built to be reused, extended, and improved by the research community. Q3 points to a paradigm shift in how computational quantum science is done. Scientists define the physics, formulate the models, and set the criteria for validation; AI agents write, test, and optimize the code. The decades-long path from a new theory to a trusted, high-performance implementation can thus collapse to days, significantly accelerating scientific discovery.

papers.title: Charge Pumping Leptogenesis from the Symmetric Mass Generation Phase on a Four-Leg Ladder Lattice
papers.abstract: Quantized charge pumping in quantum Hall systems is a bulk topological property, typically manifesting on gapless boundaries as spectral flow through chiral edge modes upon flux insertion. When the boundary is anomaly-free, it can be symmetrically gapped by symmetric mass generation (SMG) interactions. However, the effects on quantized charge pumping at an interacting gapped boundary are unclear. We address this using density-matrix renormalization group simulations of a four-leg ladder quasi-(2+1)d realization of the (1+1)d 3-4-5-0 lattice chiral fermion model with six-fermion interactions at one edge. We find gapless modes near the interacting edge for both weak and strong couplings, but the edge can be in a fully gapped SMG phase at intermediate coupling. We also identify spontaneous breaking of the model's $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry above a critical interaction strength. Across all three boundary phases, we find quantized charge pumping with the same pumped charge per flux quantum. The spatial distribution of the pumped charge varies between phases. Besides charge pumping, we study how a single injected fermion propagates under open boundary conditions. In the SMG phase, an interaction-induced flavor-mixing current develops at the endpoints of the gapped edge, which is absent in the weak- and strong-coupling limits. This current reveals a charge-redistribution mechanism unique to the SMG phase. Additionally, we propose an analogy between charge pumping in this model and a topological leptogenesis scenario in the (3+1)d Standard Model. The anomaly-free chiral U(1) symmetries of the 3-4-5-0 model play a role analogous to the baryon-minus-lepton symmetry of the Standard Model. In both settings, charge pumping can be associated with a continuous deformation along a classically defined but quantum-anomalous direction, while a discrete subgroup remains an exact quantum symmetry.

papers.title: Drying kinematics selects open honeycomb fold networks on solvent-extracted viscoelastic thin films and gels
papers.abstract: Solvent extraction and drying of substrate-supported viscoelastic films and gels produce quasiperiodic networks of three-armed surface folds. In this Letter, we examine the physical mechanisms governing their formation, length scales, and geometric organization. We observed that swelling-induced compression in the pinned film drives localized folding of a stiffening, diffusively thickening surface skin over a drained underlayer. Combining experiments and theory, we reveal that both the pattern wavelength and fold-arm length scale with the dried-film thickness following a power-law with an exponent 5/8, with remarkably weak dependence on elastic modulus. The folds form 120-degree junctions on a triangular lattice, defining an open honeycomb network whose pitch satisfies p = sqrt(3)(aL + g), where g is the junction gap. Notably, the folds accommodate less than 0.1% of the stored compressive strain, implicating elastocapillary arrest, rather than strain relaxation, in limiting their amplitude. These findings establish distinct geometric, kinetic, and interfacial constraints governing pattern selection in drying soft solids.

papers.title: Current-driven transient dynamics of magnetic-octupole domain walls in noncollinear antiferromagnets
papers.abstract: Current-driven magnetic-octupole domain walls in noncollinear antiferromagnets are promising for fast spintronic devices, yet their transient dynamics are not yet fully understood. Here, we investigate spin-orbit-torque-driven domain-wall motion in Mn$_\text{3}$Sn using a multipole micromagnetic framework. The three symmetry-related 60° walls exhibit equivalent current-driven dynamics, unlike their field-driven motion. For a representative 60° wall, the post-pulse motion is governed by relaxation of the current-induced rotation of the surrounding octupole domains, with a characteristic time of approximately 33 ps quantitatively captured by a uniform-domain analytic model. By resolving spatially nonuniform texture dynamics beyond this analytic description, the simulations further reveal an additional slow relaxation in a composite 180° wall associated with the relative motion of its constituent walls. The post-pulse response also varies systematically with the exchange stiffness and magnetic anisotropies. These results identify distinct domain and internal-coordinate relaxation channels and establish the intrinsic time scales governing pulse-controlled positioning of magnetic-octupole domain walls in antiferromagnetic spintronic devices.

papers.title: Generation and spectroscopic characterization of continuous-wave 148.4-nm light in strontium tetraborate
papers.abstract: Continuous-wave (CW) radiation at 148.4~nm is required to drive the $^{229}$Th isomeric transition of a solid-state nuclear clock, and frequency doubling of 296.8-nm light is its most direct source. We generate CW 148.4-nm light by random quasi-phase matching in strontium tetraborate and characterize it with a compact prism spectrometer built for the purpose. The spectrometer separates the harmonic from the pump on a CaF$_2$ prism, reads the wavelength from the rotation angle of a solar-blind photomultiplier, resolves the two lines with $δλ\approx 0.6~nm$, and yields an absolute power calibration. At room temperature the source delivers $1.9~nW$ at 148.4~nm, rising to 5.7 nW at the optimum crystal temperature. The conversion efficiency is also strongly structured in temperature: between 30 degree and 50 degree it shows several pronounced maxima, with neighbouring extrema only a few degrees apart, so that a small temperature excursion moves the output from a maximum to a minimum. These results provide practical guidance for optimizing and stabilizing 148.4-nm sources for solid-state $^{229}$Th nuclear clocks.

papers.title: Anomalies of TQFTs coupled to parameter spaces and constraints on ground-state degeneracies
papers.abstract: Anomalies of global symmetries can arise in long-range entangled quantum many-body systems and provide useful constraints on their dynamics. In this paper, we study anomalies of $d$-dimensional topological quantum field theories (TQFTs) coupled to parameter spaces and their implications for ground-state degeneracies. Specifically, we formulate anomalies as obstructions to constructing parametrized families of TQFTs. We discuss how the classification of these anomalies depends on the choice of topology on the universal $\mathrm{U}(1)$ $(d-1)$-form symmetry. In this framework, we use the projective ground-state bundle obtained by compactifying the TQFT on a spatial manifold to derive a general constraint relating its ground-state degeneracy $N$ to its torsion anomaly $ω$, expressed as $N\int_Wω\in\mathbb{Z}$ for bundles $W$ of spatial manifolds over closed surfaces. We apply this constraint to ground-state degeneracies of (2+1)-dimensional TQFTs with framing and 1-form symmetry anomalies and to obstructions to symmetry-preserving TQFTs. We also discuss implications for bordism generators and propose a conjecture on anomaly detection by manifolds fibered over surfaces.

papers.title: Relaxation speed in quenched-random force fields
papers.abstract: Disorder is commonly expected to slow down relaxation, as in glasses and disordered magnets. Here we show that this need not be the case in general, by analysing the asymptotic relaxation rate of a Brownian particle in a harmonic background potential and a quenched-random Gaussian force field with conservative and non-conservative components. Combining weak-disorder perturbation theory, random-matrix theory, and numerical solutions of the Fokker-Planck equation, we show that the outcome depends on the geometry of the background and on the properties of the random forces. We identify two distinct mechanisms that shape the relaxation speed: an effective stiffening of the background by the disorder, as previously reported in one dimension, and interactions (repulsive and attractive) between the levels of the Fokker-Planck operator. Through level attraction, a common feature of non-Hermitian operators, non-conservative driving forces pull the slowest mode towards faster ones, which facilitates faster relaxation. In anisotropic backgrounds, both effects occur at second order in the disorder strength, enabling either slower or faster relaxation. In isotropic backgrounds, level interactions dominate and the disorder affects the degenerate slowest mode already at first order. The shift is then given by the left-most eigenvalue of a Gaussian random matrix and relaxation is generically slowed down. In backgrounds whose anisotropy is comparable to the disorder strength, level attraction is most effective by merging the slowest mode with its neighbour into an oscillating complex-conjugate pair. In this case, relaxation becomes faster on average once the random forces are sufficiently non-conservative. Our results draw a nuanced picture of how disorder affects the asymptotic relaxation speed in complex systems and uncover general mechanisms that are likely to apply beyond the current setting.

papers.title: Solvable coupled cluster states in $d=\infty$ with prescribed momentum distribution
papers.abstract: Two of the most successful ideas in many-body theory, the exponential coupled cluster ansatz and DMFT, have to date developed separately. We establish a connection between them, by showing that the infinite dimensional limit of the hypercubic lattice allows the exact closed-form evaluation of static expectation values of coupled cluster wave functions, provided the cluster amplitudes admit a low-rank decomposition. As a result, evaluation errors -- a serious concern in conventional coupled cluster theory -- can be disentangled from limitations to expressivity of coupled cluster states. For this family of coupled cluster states, the cavity construction in $d\to\infty$ exactly reduces the environment of a lattice site to a Gaussian Grassmann kernel, and irreducible diagrams for one-body expectation values are found to be site-diagonal (in analogy to the DMFT self-energy). The resulting ``impurity problem" is an integral over a finite number of Grassmann variables rather than a dynamical quantum impurity problem, so that static observables derive exactly from a static self-consistency condition: a wave function counterpart of DMFT. For the simplest case of a cluster amplitude restricted to rank-one doubles, we obtain the momentum distribution in closed form. We show that any momentum distribution can be realized by a state that is the exact and unique ground state of an explicit parent Hamiltonian with a gapless single-particle tunnelling spectrum. By construction these coupled cluster states variationally recover low order perturbation theory for the Hubbard model. Their failure in the strong coupling regime near the Mott transition diagnoses a fundamental limitation of coupled cluster doubles. Intriguingly, our family of coupled cluster wave functions includes a gapless state with zero quasiparticle weight, with a momentum distribution that is completely smooth at the Fermi energy.

papers.title: Tensor cluster expansion as an efficient surrogate for multi-ACE
papers.abstract: In this work, we generalize an on-lattice tensor cluster expansion (TCE) framework to an arbitrary correlation order. We show that these generalized tensor cluster expansion features span a subspace of MACE features, suggesting that TCE features can sufficiently pre-screen MACE features for chemical diversity in alloyed transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) monolayers. We show that, using maximum-entropy subset sampling, we can empirically recover chemical diversity from MACE features using a cheaper TCE representation. We then fine-tune a multi-ACE (MACE) potential with both subsets, and use this potential to predict temperature-dependent vibrational properties in alloyed TMD monolayers with varying chemical ordering. In our approach, TCE features can be used as cheap surrogate features for pre-screening chemically rich configurations using MACE features, allowing for the more efficient finetuning of atomic cluster expansion (ACE) potentials, thus achieving a tractable prediction of finite-temperature alloy thermodynamics on modest hardware.

papers.title: Microswimmers lose by swimming selfishly
papers.abstract: At low Reynolds number, microswimmers are coupled by the flows they create, even when they are apart. The best way for each swimmer to push itself forward then depends on its neighbors, turning swimming together into a game. To study this, we optimize the shape changes of soft swimmers, alone and in pairs, with a differentiable Stokes solver. From random initial membrane motions, a lone swimmer converges to a traveling membrane wave. In a pair, the stroke of a swimmer affects its neighbor far more than the neighbor affects its own best stroke. For swimmers in line, this influence decays as $1/\ell$ with their separation $\ell$, whereas the incentive to respond decays as $1/\ell^2$. Selfish swimmers, which maximize their own payoff, respond only to the weak incentive. The cooperative gain they miss decays only as $1/\ell^2$, and their selfish adaptations leave the pair worse off than if both had kept their solitary strokes. Related swimmers, which also value the payoff of their neighbor, recover this gain, whereas competitors pay to hinder each other, both following a law that we derive analytically. Hydrodynamics alone thus makes swimming in company a social dilemma, whose outcome depends on how much the swimmers value each other.

papers.title: Shock Loading Accesses Reaction Pathways beyond Accelerated Thermolysis
papers.abstract: Thermolysis and shock loading can produce similar major stable products in energetic materials, despite different chemical evolution and reaction pathways. Here, we develop EMFF-MACE, a reactive machine-learning potential for C/H/N/O energetic materials, enabling thermolysis simulations of 20 materials and shock simulations of 10 on a common potential energy surface. Comparisons at matched normalized reaction progress reveal divergent chemical states and local structural environments. Mean reaction-state similarity decreases from 94.0% at 20% progress to 25.9% at trajectory endpoints, while 47.1-92.6% of shock local environments lie outside corresponding material-specific thermolysis reference domains. Structural and reaction-network analyses reveal enhanced intermolecular reorganization and additional association and rearrangement branches under shock loading, despite partially shared early decomposition chemistry. These findings show that loading history influences the structural states and subsequent reaction pathways accessed during decomposition, rather than merely the rate of thermolysis.

papers.title: Thermal conductivity of Lennard-Jones fluids from equilibrium thermodynamics
papers.abstract: We derive a general expression for the thermal conductivity of simple fluids within a thermodynamic transport theory (TTT) in which the Onsager coefficients of an interacting system are related to those of an ideal reference system through the ratio of the determinants of the Hessians of the relevant thermodynamic potential. The transported quantity is identified with an effective energy density proportional to the rms energy fluctuations of a small fluid cell. The result expresses the thermal conductivity as the product of its dilute-gas value and a function of equilibrium thermodynamic properties, namely the specific heats at constant density and at constant $ρT$ and the temperature derivative of the latter, with no adjustable parameters. For hard spheres, it reduces to a previously verified expression in terms of the thermodynamic factor. The theory is tested against molecular dynamics results for the Lennard-Jones (LJ) and the truncated and shifted Lennard-Jones (LJTS) fluids in the supercritical region, for densities up to $ρ^*=0.8$, using equations of state based on perturbation theory. For the LJTS fluid, the mean absolute percentage error is below 8\% for all the temperatures considered. For the LJ fluid, the predictions are compared with those of the revised Enskog theory for Mie fluids, using the same equation of state: TTT gives smaller errors at almost all temperatures, with a significant improvement at low temperatures, where the errors are reduced approximately by a factor between two and three.

english_guide.finding: Thermal conductivity is expressed as the dilute-gas value times a function of equilibrium thermodynamic properties, with no adjustable parameters; for LJTS the mean absolute percentage error is below 8%, and for LJ it is smaller than revised Enskog theory at almost all temperatures.
english_guide.question: Can thermal conductivity of interacting simple fluids be predicted from equilibrium thermodynamics alone, without adjustable parameters, and how accurate is it versus molecular dynamics and existing theory?
english_guide.evidence: Comparison with molecular dynamics for LJ and LJTS fluids in the supercritical region up to ρ*=0.8; LJTS mean absolute percentage error below 8% at all temperatures considered; LJ errors smaller than revised Enskog theory for Mie fluids at almost all temperatures, with low-temperature errors reduced by a factor between two and three.
english_guide.method: Thermodynamic transport theory (TTT) relating Onsager coefficients of an interacting system to an ideal reference via determinants of Hessians of the relevant thermodynamic potential; equations of state based on perturbation theory.
english_guide.novelty: Authors claim a general parameter-free expression for thermal conductivity that reduces to a previously verified thermodynamic-factor expression for hard spheres and is tested for LJ and LJTS fluids.

papers.title: Existence of the thermodynamic limit for the Hopfield model
papers.abstract: We prove that the quenched pressure of the Hopfield model with $K\simαN$ i.i.d. symmetric Rademacher patterns has a thermodynamic limit at every load $α\in(0,\infty)$, finite inverse temperature and uniform external field, with no replica-symmetry, order-parameter concentration or non-condensation hypothesis required. The limit is the supremum over $r$ of limiting pressures of mixed models with $r$ binary patterns in a Gaussian bulk. Via the Hubbard--Stratonovich representation we extract the finitely many patterns whose hidden coordinates exceed $δ\sqrt N$; a collective interpolation replaces the other binary patterns by Gaussian ones with error $O(δ^2)$ uniform in the volume, and convex concentration on the discrete cube controls the disorder-dependent choice of retained patterns. For the mixed models we prove a Gaussian hidden-spin truncation bound uniform in the volume and in an arbitrary Ising potential, and convergence for Gaussian bulks with finitely many site-field types, reducing to results of Ho and of Chen, Ho and Issa on non-convex vector spin glasses with compact spins. For Gaussian patterns we give an alternative proof of the existence result announced by Camilli, Contucci and Mingione, extended to a uniform field and an extra binary pattern. In both cases the pressure has exponentially small deviation probabilities and converges a.s.; internal energy and entropy converge wherever the limit is differentiable. An extra binary Mattis pattern admits a scalar variational reduction. At zero field the Rademacher pressure dominates the Gaussian one with an extra binary pattern, which dominates the pure Gaussian one. No explicit formula is given. The proofs were generated through extensive interaction with the AI models Claude (Opus~5.5) and ChatGPT (Sol~6.1), based on the problem formulation and guidance of the authors.
papers.study_overview_zh: 研究类型：理论；数学严格证明，非实验或数值模拟；研究对象：Hopfield 模型，K∼αN 个独立同分布对称 Rademacher 模式，有限逆温度与均匀外场

证据与比较：摘要给出证明链条而非数值：Hubbard–Stratonovich 表示提取隐藏坐标超过 δ√N 的有限多个模式；集体插值以误差 O(δ²)（对体积一致）替换其余二值模式；离散立方体上的凸集中控制保留模式的选择；混合模型得到对体积和任意 Ising 势一致的 Gaussian 隐藏自旋截断界。

papers.title: Generative Design and Graph Neural Network Screening of Novel Bimetallic Alloy Catalysts for the Hydrogen Evolution Reaction
papers.abstract: Identifying earth-abundant catalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is a central challenge in scalable green hydrogen production. We present a computational pipeline that couples diffusion-based generative modelling, machine-learning force-field relaxation, and graph neural network (GNN) property prediction to discover bimetallic HER catalysts beyond the structures and stoichiometries covered by existing adsorption databases. A generative model (MatterGen) is fine-tuned on bulk alloy structures labelled with their minimum hydrogen adsorption energy and steered towards adsorption energies near zero. From the generated pool we retain the stable structures that are novel bimetallic alloys: binary compositions built from the training-set metals but at stoichiometries or structures absent from that database. Each candidate's low-index facets are ranked by a machine-learning-force-field (MatterSim) surface-energy screen, and only the most stable terminations are converted into explicit slab models with hydrogen adsorbed at all high-symmetry surface sites and relaxed with the same force field. Two GNN surrogates (MEGNet and ALIGNN), trained on a high-throughput density functional theory (DFT) dataset, then screen the resulting slab candidates. Because the two models encode the local environment through different inductive biases, we retain only the alloys on which both agree, reducing the influence of any single model. This consensus screening, combined with a MatterSim energy-difference triangulation, resulted in a shortlist of near-thermoneutral bimetallic candidates. Eight are validated with plane-wave DFT, and four of them, Pd5Au, Pt5Rh, Cu5Pt3, and Pd13Ru3, bind hydrogen within the thermoneutral window. All eight alloys are dynamically stable by phonon calculations. These four alloys are highlighted as DFT-validated bimetallic HER candidates for experimental follow-up.

papers.title: Andreev-Enhanced Conductance in a Bilayer Graphene Quantum Point Contact
papers.abstract: Quantum point contacts provide a platform for probing mode-dependent Andreev reflection. Here, we demonstrate Andreev-enhanced conductance in a gate-defined bilayer graphene quantum point contact coupled to a superconducting aluminum electrode. Electrostatic gating enables sequential mode occupation, verified by normal-state conductance quantization. In the superconducting state, the conductance is enhanced within the conductance plateaus, while the enhancement decreases between plateaus, consistent with the nonlinear transmission dependence of Andreev reflection. The enhancement yields effective transmission probabilities up to 0.9, and extends over a bias window of approximately 140 $μ$V, which we associate with a proximity-induced superconducting gap, close to the gap of the aluminum film. For in-plane fields, the enhancement persists up to the critical field, and the bias window follows the spectral gap predicted by Abrikosov-Gor'kov theory. In contrast, perpendicular fields suppress the enhancement approximately linearly from zero field, deviating from homogeneous pair breaking and indicative of flux penetration.

papers.title: Magnetic control of reflectionless states and an intrinsic-mode exceptional point in a magnon-phonon coupling system
papers.abstract: Reflectionless states (RLs) and exceptional points (EPs) are hallmark singular responses of non-Hermitian systems, with potential applications in sensing, wave control, and energy manipulation. Yet, realizing and independently tuning these states in a compact integrated platform remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate two-dimensional magnetic control of RLs and EPs in an on-chip magnon-phonon system based on a FeGaB-32 degree-YX-LiNbO3 heterostructure. The magnetic-field magnitude tunes the magnon-phonon detuning, driving a low-loss reflection zero across the real-frequency axis and producing two field-tunable RLs with near-vanishing reflection. A closed contour of the experimentally measured complex S11 around the reflection-zero singularity accumulates a -2pi phase winding. Independently, rotating the magnetic field tunes the magnon-phonon coupling strength, driving the intrinsic magnon-phonon eigenmode spectrum across an exceptional point, identified by the exchange between real-part and imaginary-part eigenvalue splitting. A unified one-port input-output model connects the measured complex S11 response to the field-driven dynamics of the reflection zeros and the angle-tuned intrinsic magnon-phonon eigenmodes. These results establish a magnetically programmable non-Hermitian magnon-phonon platform for integrated wave control and compact vector magnetic sensing.

papers.title: Full-Potential Korringa Kohn Rostoker Study of Structural and Mechanical Properties in SiGeSn Alloys
papers.abstract: Accurate first-principles descriptions of open, covalently bonded crystal structures remain challenging within conventional Korringa--Kohn--Rostoker (KKR) approaches owing to the spherical approximations commonly employed for the effective crystal potential. Here, we systematically assess the recently developed full-potential KKR (KKR-FP) implementation in the open-source MuST package and demonstrate its applicability to diamond-structured group-IV semiconductors and SiGeSn alloys. Benchmark calculations for diamond-structured Si reveal substantial limitations of the conventional muffin-tin and atomic sphere approximations, whereas KKR-FP accurately reproduces the experimental equilibrium lattice parameter and bulk modulus, yielding 5.433 and 94.9 GPa. The full-potential treatment also recovers the semiconducting character of Si. Further calculations for elemental Ge and Sn establish the applicability of the approach across group-IV materials. Extending this framework to SiGeSn alloys, we investigate their composition-dependent equilibrium lattice parameters, bulk moduli, and mixing enthalpies. The calculated lattice parameters exhibit positive deviations from Vegard's law, while the bulk modulus decreases substantially with changes in alloy composition. Moreover, positive mixing enthalpies of 180.92 and 346.32 meV/atom are obtained for Si0.5Ge0.375Sn0.125 and Si0.375Ge0.25Sn0.375, respectively, indicating an energetic penalty for homogeneous alloy formation relative to the selected elemental reference states. These findings highlight the importance of nonspherical potential contributions in accurately describing open-structured semiconductors and establish KKR-FP within MuST as a promising framework for investigating the structural properties and mixing energetics of compositionally complex group-IV alloys

papers.title: Creating functional nanostructures for vortex manipulation in superconducting Bi$_\text{2}$Sr$_\text{2}$CaCu$_\text{2}$O$_\text{8+x}$ thin films via focused He ion beam irradiation
papers.abstract: Bi$_2$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+x}$ (Bi-2212) is a highly anisotropic high-temperature superconductor exhibiting unique vortex dynamics due to its layered structure. Precise nanoscale patterning of ultrathin Bi-2212 films remains challenging, limiting controlled studies of vortex pinning. Here, we employ 30 keV focused helium ion beam (He-FIB) irradiation to fabricate periodic arrays of columnar defects with 100 nm spacings in optimally-doped Bi-2212 thin films, thereby creating artificial vortex pinning centers. Magnetotransport measurements reveal pronounced vortex matching effects, evidenced by minima in magnetoresistance and peaks in critical current at commensurate magnetic fields. The angular dependence of magnetoresistance and critical current scale with an effective magnetic field, indicating strong confinement of pancake vortices along irradiation-induced tracks. These findings demonstrate the efficacy of He-FIB nanopatterning in modulating the superconducting properties in Bi-2212 thin films, providing a platform for fundamental studies of vortex matter and advancing prospects for device applications based on this highly anisotropic superconductor.

papers.title: Fano Resonance of a Magnonic Ring Resonator with a Nano-Scatterer Embedded in a Magnonic Conduit
papers.abstract: We present micromagnetic simulation of a nanoscale magnonic ring resonator coupled to a magnonic waveguide, with and without a hole embedded in the waveguide (H-NRR and NRR respectively), for realizing transformation into a Fano resonance frequency spectral lineshape from a Lorentzian one. Transmission and reflection spectra of the H-NRR and NRR have been analyzed for different structural parameters (embedded hole diameter and gap between the ring and the waveguide) and material parameters (damping factor of the ring) to achieve maximum spectral transmission magnitude variation. The obtained micromagnetic simulation results are supported by an analytical model that consists of two-tracks of wave propagation, forwards and backwards. Our findings show that H-NRR system demonstrates a monotonic dependence of spectral transmission magnitude variation against the aforementioned design parameters (gap and damping) which should provide better engineering controllability and tolerance when compared with the original NRR system. Overall, our proposed structure and study may help in building unconventional magnonic integrated circuits for sensing, data processing systems and computing.

papers.title: Spontaneous Circular Dichroism and Memory Effect from Surface Defects in Altermagnetic MnTe
papers.abstract: Altermagnetism has emerged as a new class of magnetism with vanishing magnetization and macroscopic time reversal symmetry breaking. Hexagonal MnTe is a g-wave altermagnet with a 307 K Néel temperature, large spin splitting, and an anomalous Hall effect. However, the relationship between altermagnetism and the anomalous Hall effect in MnTe remains debated. Here, using optical magnetic circular dichroism, we observe hysteresis and a memory effect in a MnTe bulk crystal below 250 K. No hysteresis is seen after polishing the bulk crystal and in thin films. We conclude that the hysteresis in magnetic circular dichroism in the bulk crystal is from surface defects. The similar temperature dependence and a sign change between circular dichroism and the anomalous Hall effect indicate that the origin of the anomalous Hall effect in transport is likely not intrinsic.

papers.title: Pair-Condensation Peak in Radio-Frequency Dimer-Projection Spectroscopy of a Unitary Fermi Gas
papers.abstract: Radio-frequency dimer-projection spectroscopy has recently emerged as a powerful probe of strongly interacting Fermi gases, yet its frequency-resolved spectrum remains largely unexplored. Here we show that the spectrum exhibits two qualitatively distinct features: a broad quasiparticle continuum governed by fermionic pairing and a sharp pair-condensation peak arising from the coherent projection of condensed Cooper pairs onto the final-state dimer. To reveal this physics, we develop a point-dimer approximation that exploits the separation between the molecular and many-body length scales and expresses the radio-frequency response directly in terms of pair correlations in the initial many-body state. Within the BCS mean-field theory, we derive the frequency-dependent spectrum, identify the microscopic transfer processes underlying its structure, and show that the continuum possesses a threshold determined by the superfluid gap. Our theory establishes radio-frequency dimer-projection spectroscopy as a unified probe of short-range correlations, fermionic pairing, and long-range coherence in strongly interacting Fermi gases.

papers.title: Dipolar Exciton Polarons in a van der Waals Homobilayer
papers.abstract: Fermi polarons exemplify how many-body interactions give rise to emergent quasiparticles, providing a fundamental framework for understanding interacting quantum matter. In electron-doped two-dimensional semiconductors, exciton polarons offer optical access to Fermi-polaron physics and electrical tunability, yet achieving stronger and more controllable exciton-electron interactions remains a key challenge. Here, we realize dipolar exciton polarons in an electrically tunable van der Waals homobilayer, where interlayer excitons with spatially separated electrons and holes act as quantum impurities carrying permanent electric dipole moments. These dipolar polarons exhibit substantially enhanced exciton-electron interactions, with binding energies more than four times those of conventional intralayer exciton polarons. We further demonstrate that Fermi-sea layer polarization provides an additional degree of freedom for controlling many-body interactions. In particular, the presence of a Fermi sea induces hybridization between oppositely oriented dipolar polarons, whereas confining the Fermi sea to a single layer suppresses this hybridization and produces orientation-selective many-body dressing. Our findings establish an experimental platform for dipolar-polaron physics in which dipole orientation and Fermi-sea layer polarization jointly govern many-body interactions, opening a route towards electrically tunable interactions and dipolar-polaron-mediated attraction between itinerant electrons.

papers.title: Evaluating Instrument-Centered AI Agents for Table-Top Science Experiments
papers.abstract: Reliable evaluation of AI agents for table-top science experiments has remained elusive because live instruments are hard to reset and share at scale, while instrument statefulness and safety constraints complicate evaluation. We introduce instrMCP and q-devBench, an evaluation stack for instrument-centered AI agents in table-top experiments. instrMCP connects coding agents to scientific instruments through the Model Context Protocol, serving as the instrument-access harness. q-devBench reconstructs 37 real experimental tasks from condensed-matter physics as virtual QCoDeS instruments covering quantum electronic transport, scanning probe imaging, and calibration workflows. q-devBench exposes reproducible failure modes in laboratory-agent systems while preserving realistic instrument-control workflows. Across a range of commercial coding-agent configurations, current systems already show substantial operational competence, satisfying 70-83% of measurement-related rubric criteria. The main bottleneck is scientific analysis, where performance falls to 28-46%. In an analysis-only ablation in which agents receive clean reference datasets without running the virtual measurement session, analysis performance improves substantially, closing roughly two thirds of the difference between the measurement and analysis scores. This suggests that much of the deficit arises from the measurement-session context, including tool-use overhead, longer context, measurement-planning decisions, and possible acquisition errors, while a residual scientific-reasoning gap remains. Together, instrMCP and q-devBench provide a practical sandbox for benchmarking, diagnosing, and improving laboratory AI harnesses, and establish a route from controlled virtual evaluation to future live-hardware validation.

papers.title: Pair density waves via interband pairing --- a perspective from superfluid weight
papers.abstract: Pair density waves (PDW) are superconducting states that exhibit a spatially modulated pairing order parameter, corresponding to Cooper pairs carrying finite center-of-mass momentum. While some recent studies have emphasized the role of quantum geometry in stabilizing PDW order in certain multiband systems, we here present a systematic investigation of an alternative, geometry-independent mechanism: PDW order driven purely by interband Cooper pairing. Using the superfluid weight (SW) as a diagnostic, we study two canonical models. The first is the classic Fulde-Ferrell model of an $s$-wave superconductor subject to a Zeeman splitting field, which realizes pure interband pairing between two rigidly shifted bands; the second is a spinless honeycomb-lattice model with nearest-neighbor $f$-wave pairing, a modified version of which was recently found to exhibit PDW instability in density-matrix renormalization-group simulations. In both models the SW receives no quantum geometric contribution at the mean-field level, yet it can be greatly suppressed or even turn negative, signaling a tendency toward pairing with spatial phase modulations. For the first model, we establish that the SW is increasingly suppressed as the Zeeman field grows, drastically turning negative upon the emergence of extensive gapless excitations, i.e., the Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces. For the honeycomb $f$-wave model, we demonstrate, both analytically and numerically, vanishing quantum-geometric SW and an invariably negative total SW. Our results thus establish the SW as a qualitative indicator of the tendency toward PDW order, and provide a microscopic rationale for the interband-pairing-driven PDW instability.

papers.title: Counting kinks and magnons with the lattice: magnetoelastic effects in Cs$_2$CoBr$_4$
papers.abstract: We report low-temperature dilatometry and ultrasound measurements on the frustrated quasi-one-dimensional antiferromagnet Cs$_2$CoBr$_4$ across the entire cascade of field-induced magnetic phase transitions. The whole phase diagram can be recovered from these lattice probes, with distinct anomalies observed at each phase boundary. Elongation along the principal chain axis is found to closely track magnetization throughout the phase diagram. This behavior is interpreted in terms of kinks in the Néel structure and magnons in the transverse-ordered magnetic-BEC phases, each carrying a fixed lattice distortion. A simultaneous analysis of ultrasound and striction data allows us to quantify the strength of magnetoelastic coupling.

papers.title: Static and dynamic density correlations of interacting active Brownian particles
papers.abstract: We develop a stochastic Dean--Kawasaki field theory to predict the static structure factor and collective intermediate scattering function of interacting active Brownian particles. Starting from the microscopic overdamped dynamics, we derive coupled stochastic equations for the density and polarization fields using an angular-moment closure. Gaussian linearization then yields closed analytical expressions for static and dynamic density correlations in terms of propulsion speed, mean number density, interaction potential, translational and rotational diffusivities. The coupling between density and polarization predicts a crossover from exponential relaxation to damped oscillations despite the absence of inertia. For Gaussian-core potential, the predictions contain no fitting parameters. Brownian dynamics simulations show quantitative agreement at low activity and long wavelengths, and reproduce the crossover behaviour. For Weeks--Chandler--Andersen potential, the nonintegrable core makes both the Fourier transform of the potential and the self-interaction correction term in the Dean--Kawasaki field theory ill-defined. We therefore introduce an approximation that replaces the interaction potential with a passive direct-correlation function fitted separately at each density and temperature. This approximation requires no additional activity-dependent fitting parameters.

papers.title: Hierarchy of Electromagnetic Gauge Field Quantum Geometries
papers.abstract: The conventional Bloch quantum geometric tensor (QGT) describes electric-dipole geometry for spatially uniform perturbations and vertical Bloch transitions. We develop a broader framework linking quantum geometry to local and nonlocal electromagnetic response in gauge-field space, placing this tensor within a hierarchy of electric and magnetic multipole quantum geometries. The intrinsic antisymmetric adiabatic response in every electromagnetic channel is a Berry curvature in the space of its conjugate fields. The field-dependent projector uniquely fixes the QGT for that channel, pairing the response curvature with a quantum metric. This construction extends to spatially nonuniform perturbations, whose finite momentum transfer induces nonvertical Bloch transitions. We explicitly construct the current--current QGT connecting Bloch states at $\mathbf{k}\pm\mathbf{q}/2$, providing a unified metric and curvature description of nonlocal current response. In the doubled Brillouin zone, tangential derivatives generate conventional momentum-space QGT multipoles, whereas normal derivatives connect finite-momentum geometry to uniform electric- and magnetic-multipole-pair QGTs. We derive this connection through second order in $\mathbf{q}$. The finite-momentum curvature governs the intrinsic nonlocal Hall response, while an inverse-frequency moment of symmetric optical absorption probes the index-symmetric metric sector.

papers.title: Microscopic structure at the morphotropic phase boundary in lead-barium meta-niobat
papers.abstract: Lead-barium niobate Pb$_{1-x}$Ba$_x$Nb$_2$O$_6$ is a tetragonal tungsten-bronze ferroelectric that exhibits enhanced functional properties near a morphotropic phase boundary separating orthorhombic and tetragonal phases. Using first-principles electronic-structure calculations combined with ab initio molecular dynamics, we investigate how Ba substitution modifies cation-site occupancy, local distortions, and polarization behavior across the solid solution. By explicitly accounting for vacancy ordering and the inequivalent $A$-site cages intrinsic to the tungsten-bronze framework, we identify the structural origin of the orthorhombic-to-tetragonal transition. Increasing Ba content progressively weakens the cooperative in-plane off-centering of Pb ions in the pentagonal channels and promotes out-of-plane displacements of Nb and $A$-site cations, leading to a rotation of the spontaneous polarization from [110] to [001]. The transition occurs near $x \approx 0.6$, in quantitative agreement with experimental phase diagrams. These results provide a microscopic interpretation of the morphotropic phase boundary in Pb$_{1-x}$Ba$_x$Nb$_2$O$_6$ and establish a clear structure-polarization relationship for tungsten-bronze ferroelectrics.

papers.title: Underdamped Stochastic Optimal Transport with Landauer boundary conditions: machine learning and analytical solution
papers.abstract: Finding optimal transport protocols for underdamped stochastic processes is a difficult yet important problem in control theory. In this paper we develop a direct method, based on machine learning, to find the optimal solution of the problem in the presence of non-linear boundary conditions, including those modelling the Landauer bit-erasure problem. The dynamics is steered from a single-peak to a double-peak distribution in position space, by only acting on a controllable external potential. The problem is highly non-linear, and analytical solutions are not available in general. We benchmark our numerical results with a perturbative expansion, which is expected to hold in a suitable overdamped limit.

papers.title: Finite-time Mpemba crossings with imperfect preparation
papers.abstract: Two preparations evolving under the same thermal Markov generator can reverse their ordering in relative entropy even when the hotter state retains a nonzero slow-mode component. We derive a sufficient finite-time crossing condition for arbitrary finite irreducible reversible systems. The condition compares the preparations' weights in the entire slowest eigenspace, including degeneracies, and gives an explicit upper bound using the separation from the next distinct decay rate. Exact finite-amplitude entropy comparisons also yield all-mode enclosures and bounds based on a retained spectrum with a controlled omitted tail. A preparation-error inequality converts finite-time sign margins into explicit probability tolerances; extensions account for temperature, generator, and stationary-reference uncertainty. We test the bounds on 2000 predefined network draws with four graph families and 4--64 states. There are 86 numerically located crossings, of which 45 satisfy the simple sufficient condition. In a selected eight-state example, retaining two nonstationary modes certifies a crossing before 1.55163, improving a certified slow-sector endpoint of 2.53951; the located crossing is near 1.26943. A reflecting diffusion in an asymmetric potential supplies a separate physical example, with systematic mesh refinement. Independent interval arithmetic certifies selected spectral bounds, finite-grid first crossings, and an entire preparation-temperature rectangle in a three-state benchmark. The theorem does not require exact slow-mode cancellation, while its numerical sharpness and detection coverage remain model dependent. These results concern relative-entropy relaxation and do not predict water-freezing times.

papers.title: Mirror-symmetry engineering of altermagnetism based on monolayer hexagonal lattices
papers.abstract: Altermagnetism (AM) is a novel collinear antiferromagnetic phase characterized by spin-polarized bands and zero net magnetization. However, realizing AM in monolayer hexagonal lattices is strongly constrained by lattice symmetry. Here, we propose a mirror-symmetry-based design principle and implementation scheme for realizing AM based on monolayer hexagonal lattices and validate it using holey graphyne (HGY) as a representative system. By examining hydrogenated nonmetal units X$-$H (X = B, C, N, P, and S) introduced along the mirror-symmetry axis and extending the analysis to N$-$F, we identify the configurations that form two antiparallel spin sublattices related by mirror reflection. The N$-$H structure forms a stable altermagnetic ground state, with a momentum-dependent spin splitting up to 148.2 meV. The magnetism originates from $π-π$ superexchange interactions, and H/F functionalization stabilizes intrinsic AM by regulating the local charge distribution. Our work offers insights into the design of light-element altermagnetic materials.

papers.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. II. Adsorption of nonmetal atoms (N, P, As, and Sb) on Ga-terminated surfaces
papers.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the adsorption processes on Ga-terminated surfaces of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. The considered adsorbates are nonmetal species, i.e., nitrogen, phosphorus, arsenic, and antimony on wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e., GaN(0001) surfaces, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e., GaP(111), gallium arsenide, GaAs(111), and gallium antimonide, GaSb (111) surfaces. The cases investigated include single adsorbed nonmetal atoms and full coverage, i.e. theta=1 of these surfaces. The calculated results include the stable sites and the energies of the single adsorbed atoms: located at H3 sites at low coverage and in on-top positions at high coverage for GaP, GaAs and GaSb. At high nitrogen coverage, the N2 admolecules are formed, weakly attached to the surface. The calculated electronic properties of the single-adatom systems include the band diagrams of the slabs in real and momentum space, the energies of the quantum states. In addition, the overlaps of the quantum states of the nonmetal adatoms and the nearest topmost surface Ga atoms are given. The full coverage data include the atomic configurations and the bond energies of the adsorbed layers. The electronic properties include the above-mentioned data for single adatoms, together with additional properties related to interactions between adsorbed atoms. The evaporation stability analysis confirms that the adatoms stabilize the topmost Ga atoms against detachment because of the high energy barrier of DE > 3 eV which is further increased to DE > 4 eV by coverage located at H3 sites. Thus, growth simulations should employ unreconstructed Ga-terminated surfaces covered by nonmetal atoms located at on-top positions.

papers.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. I. Clean surface properties
papers.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to elucidate the properties of the polar surfaces of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors, i.e., metal- and nonmetal-terminated. The systems considered were clean wurtzite gallium nitride (i.e. (0001) and (000-1) GaN surfaces), zinc blende gallium phosphide (i.e. (111) and (-1-1-1) GaP), gallium arsenide (i.e. (111) and (-1-1-1) GaAs), and (111) and (-1-1-1) GaSb surfaces. The calculated data include the crystallographic structure and the electronic states of the termination atoms on both sides, i.e. their positions, energies, and occupations. All nonmetal-terminated surfaces exhibit no reconstruction, and their broken-bond states are located in the vicinity of the valence band maxima (VBM), pinning the Fermi level. The Ga-terminated surface exhibited (4 x 4) reconstruction related to the division of termination atoms into sp3 and sp2 hybridized in proportions of 6 to 10, based on charge redistribution according to the electron counting rule (ECR). Thus, the broken-bond state is separated into two sets, occupied and empty, with the Fermi level located between them in the vicinity of the conduction band minimum (CBM).

papers.title: Potentials of individual atoms by convergent beam electron diffraction
papers.abstract: In convergent beam electron diffraction (CBED) on two-dimensional (2D) materials, the intensity distributions within the individual CBED spots map the local atomic arrangements within the probed region. In this study we demonstrate that the average intensities within the CBED spots essentially depend on the scattering parameters by a single atom, thus, offering the possibility of the direct measurement of such parameters. Scattering potential of an individual atom can be approximated by the Gaussian function and its parameters, the standard deviation and the maximal phase shift, can be recovered from the ratio of the intensities in the zero- and higher orders spots in CBED pattern. In order to demonstrate this, we simulated CBED patterns and extracted the atomic scattering parameters from such patterns. In the simulated examples, no weak phase object approximation is applied and the proposed method provides accurate results even for materials with large phase shifts up to 1.5 rad, as for example tungsten. The scattering parameters recovered from the experimental CBED patterns of graphene and twisted graphene-hBN structure show good agreement with the theoretically obtained values.

papers.title: Integer defects in active nematics of ellipsoidal Quincke rollers
papers.abstract: Transverse propulsion changes topological ordering in dense ellipsoidal Quincke rollers. Under an alternating-current electric field, a polar velocity field coexists with perpendicular nematic particle alignment. The system supports integer +1 velocity vortices with radial particle axes and -1 saddle defects. Oppositely charged defects migrate along domain walls and annihilate as polar domains merge. These results identify propulsion direction relative to particle shape as a control parameter for defect textures and collective ordering.

papers.title: Strong-Field-Driven Non-Linear Vibronic Coupling in an Asymmetric Donor-Acceptor Oligomer
papers.abstract: Understanding how nuclear motion couples to intramolecular charge transfer beyond the perturbative regime of light--matter interaction remains an open problem. We tackle this problem by investigating the electron-nuclear response of an acceptor-donor-acceptor oligomer with structural asymmetry due to the partial fluorination of an acceptor unit. Adopting real-time time-dependent density functional theory combined with Ehrenfest dynamics, we excite the systems with a resonant pulse of varying intensity, spanning the weak-, intermediate-, and strong-coupling regimes. When nuclei are clamped, field-driven charge preferentially flows from the donor to the fluorinated acceptor, with selectivity reduced upon increasing intensity. With moving ions, the early-time spatial response remains qualitatively unchanged, despite a distinct, spatially asymmetric charge redistribution. In the strong-field regime, nuclear motion preserves the preference for field-driven charge accumulation on the fluorinated acceptor, although the process takes approximately twice the time as in the fixed-nuclei scenario. Mode-resolved kinetic-energy analysis reveals that, with increasing field strength, the laser-induced nuclear response shifts from selected bond stretchings to collective low-frequency modes. These results provide a benchmark for assessing the interplay between vibronic dynamics and strong-field coupling in donor/acceptor oligomers.

papers.title: An internal mode shifts the depinning threshold of dissociated dislocations without changing universality
papers.abstract: Driven elastic manifolds exhibit a depinning transition whose large-scale behavior is governed by a nonequilibrium critical fixed point. Real interfaces, however, often possess internal degrees of freedom, raising the question of whether such modes alter depinning universality or only nonuniversal properties of the transition. We address this question for a dissociated dislocation, whose two Shockley partials define a fluctuating stacking-fault width driven by correlated random-alloy stresses. Comparing exact thresholds on identical disorder realizations with the width either free or frozen, we find that width fluctuations leave the depinning universality class unchanged: the roughness exponent $ζ$ and correlation-length exponent $ν$ remain the same even when the width becomes strongly fluctuating and locally multistable. The threshold, however, shifts. The shift is governed by the elastic crossover length of the internal mode rather than by multistability, and can have either sign. An infinite-range mean-field treatment misses this mechanism. With the physical two-partial elastic kernel and disorder calibrated against measured strengths, width fluctuations raise the athermal critical resolved shear stress by 10-35% over that of a rigid dissociated dislocation. An internal mode can thus be irrelevant at the depinning fixed point while remaining quantitatively important for where the transition occurs.

papers.title: Spin conservation protects the altermagnetic spin-splitter current from critical scattering
papers.abstract: Near a magnetic transition, critical fluctuations scatter electrons strongly, but the charge current survives, because long wavelength fluctuations barely turn the electron velocity. In an altermagnet the electric field also drives a spin current, the spin splitter effect, and a nearly forward scattering event that flips spin moves an electron to the other spin band at almost unchanged velocity. We show that the spin current shares the protection of the charge current only when the fluctuations conserve spin. Solving the Boltzmann equation with the full collision operator, including its change with the magnetic order, we find that forward flips equalize the two spin populations at equal energy at the quasiparticle rate, which in two dimensions grows linearly with the correlation length, whereas spin conserving fluctuations relax the spin current at a rate comparable to the charge relaxation rate. Fluctuations with the same resistivity can thus move the spin splitter ratio in opposite directions. Energy conservation protects the part of the spin current that follows the band shift of the occupied states, and the splitting blocks forward flips once the spin Fermi lines lie farther apart than the inverse correlation length. A disorder series at fixed reduced temperature measures the initial fall of the ratio with the magnetic resistivity independent of the order amplitude, and the growth of this slope toward the transition identifies spin flip critical fluctuations.

papers.title: Spin-conserving and spin-flip magnetic scattering in the altermagnetic spin-splitter effect
papers.abstract: Critical magnetic fluctuations scatter electrons strongly near an ordering transition, but they barely degrade the charge current, because they scatter mostly through small angles. In an altermagnet the electric field also drives a spin current, and a nearly forward spin flip moves an electron to the other spin band at almost unchanged velocity. We develop a Boltzmann theory of the spin splitter ratio that keeps the full collision operator of quasistatic magnetic fluctuations and its change with the magnetic order. Fluctuations of equal total strength give the same resistivity for every fraction of spin flips, yet they can move the spin splitter ratio in opposite directions. Spin conserving fluctuations relax the spin current at about the charge relaxation rate, whereas forward flips equalize the two spin populations at equal energy at the quasiparticle rate, which in two dimensions grows linearly with the correlation length. Energy conservation on the split bands protects the part of the spin current carried by the band shift of the occupied states at every scattering strength, and the splitting blocks forward flips once the spin Fermi lines lie farther apart than the inverse correlation length. When flips dominate, a quarter to a half of the lattice band ratio survives. The transport time approximation reproduces the initial growth of the resistivity but recovers only a quarter to a half of the initial fall of the ratio, and a disorder series at fixed reduced temperature measures this fall independent of the order amplitude.

papers.title: Multiband-Induced Complex Magnetotransport in the Kagome Metal LuNb$_6$Sn$_6$
papers.abstract: We report the electrical transport properties of the kagome metal LuNb$_6$Sn$_6$, which undergoes a charge density wave (CDW) transition at $T_\mathrm{CDW}\approx80$ K. Similar to the kagome metals $A$V$_3$Sb$_5$ ($A$ = K, Rb, Cs), LuNb$_6$Sn$_6$ develops complex magnetotransport behavior near and below the CDW transition. In particular, the longitudinal magnetoconductivity exhibits an approximately linear field dependence below about 1 T, whereas the field dependence of Hall conductivity displays pronounced nonlinearity and a field-induced sign reversal. Although an anomalous Hall-like contribution can be extracted by subtracting a local background from the Hall conductivity, mobility-spectrum analysis shows that the overall magnetotransport can be largely accounted for by multiband conduction involving high-mobility electronlike and holelike carriers. Nevertheless, sizable deviations from the multiband model emerge near $T_{\mathrm{CDW}}$, pointing to additional CDW-related scattering processes. These results demonstrate that high-mobility multiband transport, together with CDW-induced modifications of carrier scattering, play important roles in the complex magnetotransport of LuNb$_6$Sn$_6$.

papers.title: Airy distribution of the quenched spectral form factor in non-interacting fermions
papers.abstract: For chaotic many-body systems as well as the random energy model, the logarithm of the (scaled) spectral form factor (SFF) exhibits two robust properties at late times: (i) self-averaging and (ii) a reflected-Gumbel distribution. Here, we demonstrate that both properties break down for $N$ non-interacting fermions on a lattice of size $L$ with an incommensurate single-particle spectrum. We show that the logarithm of the SFF, upon rescaling by $1/\sqrt{L}$, follows the Airy distribution, in stark contrast to the reflected-Gumbel law. Moreover, it is no longer self-averaging, as its mean and standard deviation are of the same order. While deviations from reflected-Gumbel statistics are generically expected for non-interacting systems, we find that an interacting integrable model exhibits reflected-Gumbel statistics at late times, mirroring the chaotic case and distinguishing it from non-interacting fermions.

papers.title: Agentic Global Optimization of Site-Disordered Crystalline Materials
papers.abstract: Site-disordered crystals, in which several elements partially occupy the same atomic site, cannot be simulated atomistically without first resolving an explicit ordering, and the number of possible orderings grows combinatorially with supercell size. Because each candidate requires an expensive structural relaxation, locating the global-minimum ordering is a costly combinatorial search. Here, we present an agentic search in which a surrogate model, fitted to previously evaluated configurations, selects each subsequent candidate by balancing exploitation, uncertainty, and novelty. Four surrogates are implemented within a shared framework: an ExtraTrees ensemble, Bayesian ridge regression, sparse ARD regression, and an ALiEGNN-inspired graph ensemble. These are benchmarked against three traditional methods: random walk, Markov chain Monte Carlo, and a genetic algorithm across 14 test cases spanning 12 crystal structures, with exhaustively enumerated global minima as ground truth. The agentic surrogates reach the global minimum in 94% of runs, compared with 55% for the traditional methods, with a median 4.3-fold reduction in evaluations relative to the best traditional method. Bayesian ridge regression succeeds in all runs with the fewest evaluations. Applied to Na2/3FePO4, with coupled Na/vacancy configurational disorder and Fe2+/Fe3+ charge disorder, the framework recovers the experimentally reported ordering when charge states are encoded in the surrogate representation, demonstrating its extension to multi-sublattice disorder.

papers.title: Only the immortal can (almost) flock while turning: Two-dimensional chiral immortal flocks, time crystals and non-universal sub-logarithmic roughness
papers.abstract: We study two-dimensional chiral ``dry'' (non-momentum conserving) ``immortal'' (number conserving) ``flocks'' (polar ordered active fluids). Noise driven fluctuations about the noise-free ``time crystal'' state, in which the velocity rotates uniformly in time, obey coupled Kardar-Parisi-Zhang-like equations for the local velocity orientation and a conserved concentration field; the latter field stabilizes order. Orientational fluctuations grow only sub-logarithmically, and number fluctuations are suppressed (``hyperuniform''); both exhibit nonuniversal scaling exponents. There are three different universality classes of disordering transitions.

papers.title: Quantifying Blinking Suppression and Probing Its Mechanism in PPD-Treated Single Quantum Dots
papers.abstract: Colloidal semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) are highly promising materials for various applications, yet photoluminescence intermittency (blinking) remains a key obstacle to their practical use. While recent advances have enabled partial or complete suppression of this effect, both the degree of suppression and the mechanism by which it occurs are often difficult to establish. In the present work we analyse the blinking suppression of single CdSe/ZnS QDs after treatment with p-phenylenediamine (PPD), recently discovered by Yang et al. We revisit the blinking mechanism in this system and show that it is governed predominantly by the trapping mechanism, rather than by Auger ionization as previously proposed. For data analysis we apply a threshold-free two-dimensional criterion recently proposed by Podshivaylov and Frantsuzov. The criterion is based on the relative quantum yield estimator $\langle \hat{Q} \rangle^{(s)}$ and the decay-rate fluctuation parameter $\hatξ$. We found that PPD treatment significantly increases the relative quantum yield and leads to only a modest increase in $\hatξ$, indicating that the dominant effect of PPD is to shift the distribution of the non-radiative recombination rate toward lower values, rather than to eliminate its fluctuations. We further suggest a number of possible mechanisms of PPD-induced suppression and propose critical experiments for their verification.

papers.title: Coordination three heals, coordination four is hard: the antiferromagnetic Potts model with a costly third state
papers.abstract: We study the ground states of the antiferromagnetic three-state Potts model in which the third state carries a single-ion energy cost $D_3$, on arbitrary lattices, and show that the difficulty of the ground-state problem is controlled by the maximum coordination $Δ$ alone; on planar lattices with $Δ\le5$ it is classified completely. On lattices with coordination at most three the third state heals frustrated bonds one for one: every graph of maximum degree three other than $K_4$ has an independent set of sites that meets every odd cycle and whose size equals the number $\operatorname{fr}$ of frustrated bonds of the Ising ground state. This identity also follows from known results on the chromatic vertex stability of graphs; we give a constructive proof. Hence $E_0 (D_3)=\min(D_3,1) \operatorname{fr}$ for all $D_3$, computable in polynomial time on planar lattices. In graph-theoretic terms, independent odd cycle transversal is solvable in polynomial time on planar subcubic graphs. On planar lattices with maximum coordination four, in contrast, deciding the ground-state energy is NP-complete for every fixed $0\le D_3<2$ and polynomial for $D_3\ge2$. The boundary is set by a local principle: a site of coordination $d$ in the third state relieves at most $\lfloor d/2\rfloor$ frustrated bonds, so the third state is useless once $D_3\ge\lfloorΔ/2\rfloor$; this threshold is sharp for every $Δ\ge3$ and reproduces the triangular-lattice point $D_3^*=3$ of the equivalent spin-1 Blume--Capel antiferromagnet. From a single Ising ground state the proof builds an exact ground state in polynomial time, which for quasicrystalline, foam-like and defective lattices with thousands of sites takes seconds to minutes.

papers.title: Berry curvature quadrupole induced third-order anomalous Hall effect in altermagnetic $\mathrm{KV_2Se_2O}$
papers.abstract: Altermagnets combine compensated magnetic order with momentum-dependent spin splitting, providing a symmetry-rich platform for exploring nonlinear quantum-geometric transport. In the d-wave altermagnet considered here, the antiunitary symmetry operation $TC_{4z}$ enforces a vanishing momentum-integrated Berry curvature, while inversion symmetry forbids a finite Berry-curvature dipole. Consequently, the Berry curvature quadrupole (BCQ) can provide a contribution to the nonlinear Hall response, scaling as $τ^2$, where $τ$ denotes the relaxation time. We derive a gauge-covariant Wannier interpolation formula that enables efficient evaluation of the BCQ directly from first-principles Wannier tight-binding Hamiltonians. Applying this framework to $\mathrm{KV_2Se_2O}$, we calculate the momentum-space distribution of the BCQ and the associated chemical potential dependent nonlinear conductivity. The momentum-resolved analysis reveals that the dominant contribution originates from spin-orbit coupling induced avoided arossings, directly linking the gap structure to the sign-changing nonlinear response. Our work establishes a general first-principles route to higher-order quantum-geometric responses in altermagnets, opening avenues for exploring nonlinear Hall effects in next-generation spintronic and magnetoelectronic devices.
